title: Multiplying flow and pressure — data and interactive review tool for the detection of respiratory phases in intra-arrest ventilation
description:
Data and an interactive review interface accompanying the article Multiplying flow and pressure: detecting respiratory phases in intra-arrest ventilation (Resuscitation, 2026;222:111050).

The article proposes an algorithm that detects respiratory phases and their exact onsets during ventilation with ongoing chest compressions, using the product of airflow and airway pressure for inspiration and the product of airflow and the slope of airway pressure for expiration. It was validated against investigator-established ground truth on ventilatory recordings from 13 pigs: for each animal, 20 ventilations before induction of cardiac arrest (regular ventilation) and 20 ventilations delivered asynchronously during ongoing mechanical chest compressions (intra-arrest ventilation), amounting to 606 s of regular and 1420 s of intra-arrest ventilation.

Each of the 13 cases is one experiment day, stored as a serialised vitabel Vitals object. Every case holds two recording segments, one per ventilation condition, each carrying airway flow, airway pressure and the two products, together with annotation labels for the experimental phase, the investigator-established ground-truth onsets and intervals, and the onsets detected by the algorithm.

The repository ships a Voilà review interface and a conda environment, so the annotations can be inspected breath by breath without local installation.

Licensing. The recordings are licensed under CC BY 4.0, which requires attribution: please credit the article above. The review notebook and the configuration files are licensed under the MIT licence.

Experiments were conducted between November 2022 and January 2023 at the experimental anaesthesia laboratory of the Medical University of Innsbruck, authorised by the Austrian Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF-V/3b GZ:2021-0.895.386). The experiments complied with Austrian and European regulations concerning the use of laboratory animals.
